details: @jexkcode/baileys is a combosquat of the WhiskeySockets/Baileys WhatsApp Web API library: it ships forked Baileys source under an unofficial scope while keeping the canonical basename "baileys", so installs of the real package can be redirected to it by a single character in the scope. The fork adds a non-consensual channel autofollow. lib/Socket/index.js calls setupAutoFollow(sock, newConfig) unconditionally for every socket created by makeWASocket(), and lib/Utils/auto-follow.js — presented as a "fallback" — calls sock.newsletterFollow('120363405612723183@newsletter') three seconds after each connection.update event reports an open connection. The only guard is a private sock.__channelFollowed boolean; the configuration option the code comment describes is never read, failures are swallowed by an empty catch handler, and the follow therefore happens silently on every WhatsApp account the library operates. The package also declares the lifecycle hook "preinstall": "node./engine-requirements.js", whose content only checks the Node.js version and exits on unsupported releases. Outbound network destinations in the shipped code are wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat for the WhatsApp protocol, hxxps://call[.]whatsapp[.]com for call links, and an opt-in OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint in lib/Utils/transcribe.js whose API key the caller supplies; the package's auth-state modules (lib/Utils/use-single-file-auth-state.js, use-multi-file-auth-state.js, use-sqlite-auth-state.js) only read and write the caller's own credential file locally. No hardcoded command-and-control endpoint, no downloader, and no code-execution primitive (eval, Function constructor, atob) is present. The concrete abuse vector is the hardcoded channel JID 120363405612723183@newsletter, which makes every integrating deployment recruit its users into that channel.
